preconditions.expression: root is None or isinstance(root, TreeNode)
preconditions.description: The input `root` is either a `TreeNode` instance or `None`, representing an empty tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= node.val <= 10**5 for node in [root] + [n for n in stack if n is not None] if isinstance(node, TreeNode))
preconditions.description: Every node's value in the tree (including `root` and all reachable nodes) satisfies 1 ≤ node.val ≤ 10^5. This is implicitly true if the tree is constructed correctly.

postconditions.expression: return_value == [] if root is None else return_value
postconditions.description: If the input tree is empty (`root` is `None`), the output is an empty list. Otherwise, the output is a non-empty list.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= val <= 10**5 for val in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every value in the output list satisfies 1 ≤ val ≤ 10^5, matching the constraints of node values.
The length of the output list equals the number of nodes in the tree, where `preorder_iterative(root)` is the correct preorder traversal sequence (Root->Left->Right) generated iteratively.

postconditions.expression: return_value == [root.val] + preOrder(root.left) + preOrder(root.right) if root is not None else []
postconditions.description: The output list is the preorder traversal of the tree, defined recursively as `[root.val] + preOrder(root.left) + preOrder(root.right)` for a non-empty tree. This must hold even though the implementation is iterative.
